title: TOEFL iBT Reading Practice Test 11
instructions: Read each passage carefully and answer all questions. You have 35 minutes. Questions test factual understanding, vocabulary, inference, and the ability to identify main ideas.

passages.title: Wetland Ecosystems and Biodiversity
passages.text:
Wetland Ecosystems and Biodiversity is an important subject of modern scientific and scholarly investigation. Researchers have identified several key mechanisms that govern how this phenomenon operates and how it has changed over time.

Early studies of wetland ecosystems and biodiversity focused on descriptive accounts, but more recent work employs quantitative methods that allow more precise measurement of patterns and processes. This shift has led to more reliable conclusions that can be applied to real-world problems.

The environmental and social implications of wetland ecosystems and biodiversity are considerable. Changes in conditions can affect biodiversity, human health, economic systems, and cultural practices in ways that researchers are still working to quantify and understand fully.

Technological advances have accelerated progress in understanding wetland ecosystems and biodiversity. Remote sensing, genetic analysis, computational modelling, and international research collaborations have all contributed to a more nuanced picture of the subject.

Policymakers and practitioners increasingly draw on research about wetland ecosystems and biodiversity to inform decisions about conservation, public health, urban planning, and resource management. The challenge lies in translating scientific findings into effective action at both local and global scales.

questions.prompt:
Insert the sentence — "The light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes and generate the energy carriers needed for subsequent carbon fixation." — into the paragraph. The four squares [1] [2] [3] [4] show where it could be added; choose the best position.

Plants convert sunlight into chemical energy through a complex process involving light and dark reactions.

[1] During photosynthesis, chlorophyll molecules in plant leaves absorb light energy and transfer it to electrons. [2] These energized electrons move through the thylakoid membrane, creating an electrochemical gradient that drives ATP synthesis. [3] The Calvin cycle then uses this ATP and NADPH to reduce carbon dioxide into glucose. [4] This process is responsible for the vast majority of organic matter production on Earth and serves as the foundation for nearly all food webs.
questions.explanation: The sentence must follow the introduction of light energy transfer (at position 2) and logically precedes the Calvin cycle explanation. It bridges the light reactions and dark reactions with the connector 'generate' that refers to energy carrier production needed later.

questions.prompt:
Insert the sentence — "The symbiotic relationship between corals and zooxanthellae—algae living within coral cells—enables them to thrive in nutrient-poor tropical waters." — into the paragraph. The four squares [1] [2] [3] [4] show where it could be added; choose the best position.

Coral reefs are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth, supporting extraordinary biological diversity.

[1] Although coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor, they harbor approximately 25% of all known marine fish species. [2] These underwater structures are built by coral polyps, which create calcium carbonate skeletons that accumulate into massive reef formations. [3] The reef environment provides shelter, food sources, and breeding grounds for thousands of species including fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and echinoderms. [4] Regrettably, rising ocean temperatures and acidification pose severe threats to reef health and survival.
questions.explanation: This sentence explains how corals create the reef environment mentioned in position 2. The word 'them' refers to corals, and the ecological mechanism logically precedes the discussion of benefits that reefs provide in position 3.
